items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Maurice told him to meet us at the Church on Quai d'Orsay. He was a newspaper reporter from the States that came to Paris soon after the war finished. He wrote for the 'Chicago Defenser'and his name was Ollie Stewart.

ctx.x: Finally, the ceremony began without a photographer. At one time, the Mayor said something which I did not understand because my French was no hell. There was a silence and then I decided to say 'oui'(wee in French) and I hit the right note. I was expecting Sacha to give me a hint, as we do in the States, when I was to say 'oui', but that didn't happen so I played it by ear and came out right at the coda.

After the civil ceremony we went to a cafe very near to have a celebration drink and Maurice went in the telephone booth again to try to find a photographer. He finally found one and Maurice told him to meet us at the Church on Quai d'Orsay. He was a newspaper reporter from the States that came to Paris soon after the war finished. He wrote for the 'Chicago Defenser'and his name was Ollie Stewart.

The priest - Reverent William, had insisted of giving us a lecture before the ceremony. He asked Lily if she was aware of the problems created by interracial marriage,especially if we had to go back to live in the U.S.A. 'Yes' said Lily, she was.
